name: sponsor
title: Sponsor
description: A presentation slot the host fills, and obviously not the game. BDS-043: the sponsor's brand is the sponsor's, so the logo is a node the host passes and the library applies no token to it. Nothing here tints, crops, re-colours or animates it, and no theme reaches inside the slot. It carries `data-gs-component="sponsor"` and nothing else in the namespace, which is the contract: no `data-gs-selected`, `data-gs-committed`, `data-gs-state`, `data-gs-disabled`, `data-gs-locked` or `data-gs-animates`, because a slot carrying any of those would be styled as part of the game. The five lockups, inline, hud, reward, interstitial and badge, are classes and sizes rather than attributes for the same reason. The label is required and is what keeps the slot honest: a logo with no "Presented by" above it is an advert nobody was told about. It is not a link, because the library's perform-nothing boundary forbids building a link target from a prop; a host that wants a clickable sponsor wraps this in its own anchor.

files.content:
'use client' import * as React from 'react' // The component brings its own styles. Without this a `gamestage-ui add` installs a // working but completely unstyled Sponsor, and `tsc --noEmit` passes on it, so // the gate cannot catch it. import './sponsor.css' /** * Sponsor: a presentation slot the host fills, and obviously not the game. * * BDS-043: the sponsor's brand is the sponsor's. The logo is a node the host * passes and the library applies no token to it, so no theme re-colours it, no * theme re-shapes it, and nothing here tints, crops or animates it. * * The attribute contract says it carries `data-gs-component="sponsor"` and that * is all, and the absence is deliberate. It is not a control, so it carries no * `data-gs-selected`, `data-gs-committed`, `data-gs-state`, `data-gs-disabled` * or `data-gs-locked`, and it is not a game element, so it carries no * `data-gs-animates`. A sponsor slot that gained any of those would be styled * as part of the game, which is the thing a sponsor's brand guidelines exist to * prevent. The five slots are classes rather than attributes for the same * reason. * * The label is required, and it is what keeps the slot honest. "Presented by", * "Timed by", "Prize from": a logo with no line above it is a logo pretending * to be game furniture, and a player who cannot tell the difference has been * shown an advert without being told it was one. * * The plate is the one thing here that is drawn and not themed. Specimen 4g * writes the rule beside the lockups: "plate: auto|light|dark", "logo never * tinted, never on gradient", and draws every logo on a white plate. So the * plate is white or black, chosen by the host for the logo's contrast, and it * takes no token: a theme that could reach the plate could put a sponsor's * mark on a gradient, which is the thing the rule forbids. * * It is not a link. The design names an optional `url` and the library's * perform-nothing boundary forbids building a link target from a prop, so a * host that wants a clickable sponsor wraps this in its own anchor and owns the * navigation. */ export type SponsorSlot = 'inline' | 'hud' | 'reward' | 'interstitial' | 'badge' /** The plate under the logo: white, black, or none when the asset brings its own. */ export type SponsorPlate = 'light' | 'dark' | 'none' export interface SponsorProps extends React.HTMLAttributes { /** * Which lockup this is. `inline` is the presented-by line, `hud` attaches to * a timer or score chip, `reward` sits inside a prize card, `interstitial` * fills the gap between rounds, `badge` is the smallest mark. Each is a size * and a shape; none of them is a colour. */ slot?: SponsorSlot /** The relationship, in words: "Presented by", "Timed by", "Prize from". */ label: string /** The sponsor's name. Always readable, whether or not a logo renders. */ name: string /** * The sponsor's own asset, as a node. Untouched: the library sets its size * box and nothing else. Absent renders the name as text, which is a sponsor * credit rather than a gap. */ logo?: React.ReactNode /** * The plate the logo sits on. The host picks it for the logo's contrast, as * the design says; the library never picks it from the theme. `light` is * what specimen 4g draws everywhere. */ plate?: SponsorPlate /** * What the host shows under the lockup: the interstitial's "Next round in * 0:05", which the design says it always carries. Host state, host markup. */ children?: React.ReactNode } export function Sponsor({ slot = 'inline', label, name, logo, plate = 'light', className, children, ...rest }: SponsorProps) { return (
{label} {logo ? ( <> {logo} {/* The name is in the accessible name whatever the logo does, because a sponsor credit nobody can read is not a credit. */} {name} ) : ( {name} )} {children === undefined || children === null ? null : ( {children} )}
) }

docs: Pass `label` as the relationship in words, `name` as the sponsor's name, and `logo` as the sponsor's own asset. The asset arrives on screen exactly as you gave it: the component sets its height box and nothing else, so any plate, padding or background the brand guidelines require travels with the asset rather than being invented here. Pick `slot` for where it sits: `inline` for a presented-by line, `hud` beside a timer or score chip, `reward` inside a prize card, `interstitial` between rounds, `badge` for the smallest mark. Show one sponsor per screen, the interstitial excepted. Leave `logo` out when you have no asset and the name renders as the credit. Wrap it in your own anchor if it has to be clickable.
